newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea offers help to N.Korea if policies changed.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea offers help to N.Korea if policies changed.

text.p: South Korean President Kim Young-sam on Friday offered to help rescue communist North Korea from economic ruin if it agreed to change its military-oriented policies.

"If North Korea chooses the path of change, we have the will and capability to cooperate with it as much as it wants," Kim said in a speech marking the 52nd anniversary of Korea's independence from Japanese colonial rule.
The South Korean president said although there had been setbacks, relations between the two Koreas were "clearly making progress".

He noted that the two Koreas, along with the United States and China, held four-nation talks in New York last week to arrange formal negotiations aimed at setting up a permanent peace mechanism on the Korean peninsula.
Senior officials from the four countries failed to set an agenda for the formal peace talks but agreed to meet again on September 15 in New York.

Kim said Seoul would help Pyongyang improve ties with its allies. "Of course, this has to be preceded by a change in North Korea's attitude: it must behave reasonably as a responsible member of the international community."
